operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
1. There is established in the Office
for Emergency Management of the Ex­
ecutive Office of the President the Phil­
ippine Alien Property Administration, 
at the head of which shall be a Philip­
pine Alien Property Administrator ap­
pointed by the President, without regard 
to the civil service laws. The Philippine 
Alien Property Administrator shall re­
ceive compensation at such rate as the 
President shall approve and in addition 
shall be entitled to actual and necessary 
transportation, housing, subsistence, 
and other expenses incidental to the 
performance of his duties. Within the 
limitation of such funds as may be made 
available for that purpose, and without 
regard to the civil service laws, the 
Philippine Alien Property Administrator 
may appoint assistants and other per­
sonnel and delegate to them such func­
tions as he may deem necessary to carry 
out the provisions of this order. Such 
personnel of the Office of Alien Property 
Custodian as are engaged in the exer­
cise of the functions transferred here­
under, may be transferred to the Philip­
pine Alien Property Administration 
without loss of such civil service status 
or eligibility therefor as they may 
possess.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 9818 contains no savings clause for EO 9789, but it re-establishes the same Philippine Alien Property Administration in the Office for Emergency Management with the same functions (its paragraphs 1-8 track EO 9789's, now naming the Attorney General as the Custodian's successor), so the Administration, its personnel and the property already transferred to it under EO 9789 between October 14, 1946 and January 7, 1947 carried on under EO 9818's own terms. Those transfers are accrued results; the continuing authority after January 7, 1947 is EO 9818's, not EO 9789's. Paragraph 7's amendment of EO 9142 is likewise restated in EO 9818 paragraph 7.

research_rationale: EO 9789 of October 14, 1946 (official text 11 FR 11981, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line, F.R. Doc. 46-18658) establishes the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defines its functions in nine paragraphs; it takes effect October 14, 1946 (paragraph 9). The text is printed across columns interrupted by the issue's contents and codification guide, so paragraph 2 is inventoried in two quoted parts (before and after the interruption); no other text belongs to the order. EO 9788, signed the same day (F.R. Doc. 46-18657) and effective October 15, 1946, terminated the Office of Alien Property Custodian and moved its functions to the Attorney General; it is recorded as a later event on the clauses that direct the Custodian to act, because it changed who performed them without ending them. EO 9818 of January 7, 1947 (12 FR 133, read in full) re-issues the order with changes and in paragraph 9 provides 'This order supersedes Executive Order ... of October 14, 1946, entitled "Establishing the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defining its functions."' (OCR prints the number '928.9'; the date and title identify EO 9789). EO 9818 states no effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1947-01-07. This resolves the draft's undated-ending conflict. No earlier end was found: EO 9789 has no expiry or condition, no evidence shows any directive was fully performed before supersession, and the OFR catalog, the saved-text corpus and the U.S. Code/eCFR hits (historical notes) show no other event. All clauses first ended 1947-01-07, the whole-order end. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text, not compared with page images.
